qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Canadian Big 6 banking oligopoly protected by OSFI regulatory barriers, entrenched branch networks, and low-cost core deposit switching costs. Consistently delivers 12-14% return on equity across credit cycles.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 6 (gate_6_cash_and_balance_sheet = N). While BMO enjoys a protected Canadian oligopoly and steady multi-decade returns, its fractional-reserve banking model relies on 12-15x balance sheet leverage, credit cycle exposure, and wholesale deposit funding that inherently fails the Munger peace-of-mind fortress balance sheet standard.
qualitative.evidence: BMO is Canada's 4th largest bank by assets, operating across Canadian P&C, US P&C (BMO Harris / Bank of the West), Wealth Management, and Capital Markets. Despite solid historical ROE (~12-14%) and OSFI CET1 ratio >13%, its commercial banking model operates with CAD $163.6B in long-term debt against CAD $8.3B net income (>19x debt/income) and interest coverage of only 1.27x. Inherent fractional-reserve duration mismatch and credit cycle risk fail Gate 6 by design.

evaluation_metadata.verdict: Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet
